intro: This branch applies math to physical motion and forces: falling objects, things sliding on slopes, pulleys and balancing beams.

VI.12.01.what: Reading motion from graphs, where the steepness and the area under the line each tell part of the story.

levels.a: Finds velocity from the steepness (gradient) of a position–time graph.
levels.b: Finds acceleration from the steepness of a velocity–time graph.
levels.c: Finds displacement from the area under a velocity–time graph.
levels.d: Distinguishes total distance traveled from change in position.

VI.12.02.what: A set of five equations (often called "suvat") for objects speeding up or slowing down at a steady rate.

levels.a: Knows the constant-acceleration equations and what each letter means.
levels.b: Chooses the right equation from the information given.
levels.d: Handles journeys with two stages, like speeding up then braking.

VI.12.03.what: Modeling objects thrown straight up or dropped, with gravity pulling them down.

levels.a: Uses gravity as a steady downward acceleration.
levels.b: Models an object thrown up that falls back down.
levels.d: Finds the total time spent in the air.

VI.12.04.what: Newton's laws describe how forces change motion. A bigger push gives a bigger acceleration.

levels.a: Identifies weight, the surface's push back (normal reaction) and string tension.
levels.b: Combines forces into one overall (resultant) force.
levels.c: Uses force equals mass times acceleration.
levels.d: Applies the third law: every push has an equal push back.

VI.12.05.what: Splitting a slanted force into sideways and up-down parts, which makes problems much easier.

levels.a: Splits a force into two parts using sine and cosine.
levels.b: Uses balanced forces (equilibrium) to find unknowns.
levels.c: Handles objects resting or moving on a slope.
levels.d: Finds an unknown force from the other forces present.

VI.12.06.what: Objects linked by strings or rods, like two weights over a pulley, that move together.

levels.a: Finds the tension (pulling force) in a connecting string.
levels.c: Solves for the shared acceleration of the linked objects.
levels.d: Models lifts and vehicles towing trailers.

VI.12.07.what: Friction is the grip between surfaces that resists sliding. It has a maximum strength that depends on how hard the surfaces press together.

levels.a: Uses the rule that friction is at most a constant times the normal reaction.
levels.b: Identifies limiting friction, when an object is just about to slip.
levels.c: Includes friction for objects on a slope.
levels.d: Decides whether an object will slide or stay put.

VI.12.08.what: Modeling the curved path of a thrown or kicked object by treating sideways and up-down motion separately.

levels.a: Splits the motion into horizontal and vertical parts.
levels.b: Finds how long the object stays in the air.
levels.c: Finds how far it travels and how high it goes.
levels.d: Chooses the launch speed or angle to hit a target.

VI.12.09.what: A moment is the turning effect of a force, like pushing a door far from its hinge versus close to it.

levels.a: Finds a moment as force times the perpendicular distance to the pivot.
levels.b: Balances turning effects on a level rod.
levels.c: Handles a rod just on the point of tipping over.
levels.d: Finds the force needed from a support.
